recommendations: Move frequently used tools and materials to point-of-use storage at each station to eliminate locker and retrieval delays.
Implement preventive calibration checks before production starts, especially at Station 2, to avoid mid-batch stoppages.
Define a single owner and queue for rework, with visual controls that distinguish rework from normal flow.
Add SKU and special-handling verification steps before material delivery and before packing/picking begins.
Provide a cart or multi-bin carrier for the material handler to reduce redundant trips.
Address the single-dock bottleneck with scheduled delivery windows or additional dock capacity if inbound volume warrants it.
Keep inventory updates synchronized in real time so physical putaway and system records match before picking starts.
Formalize backup coverage for quality inspection and require physical segregation of inspected versus uninspected boards.
Restrict cross-role task help to trained personnel only, or provide quick task-specific training for temporary assistance.
Consider formalizing effective pre-shift readiness work, including tool setup, printer prep, and material staging, and decide whether it should be paid or scheduled time.
Move frequently used tools to point-of-use storage at each station to eliminate locker-retrieval delay.
Restrict cross-role assistance unless the worker is trained on the specific task and conventions.
Provide a short, standardized convention guide or visual cue set for any temporary cross-role assistance.
